title: Sirdars, grandees and maharajahs
html_source:
a comic over-statement of Irish representatives

Sirdar: a variant of Sardar, a long-standing rank in Western and Southern Asia – was assigned to the British Commander-in-Chief of the British-controlled Egyptian Army in the late 19th century
Grandee: a Spanish or Portuguese nobleman of the highest rank.
Mahārāja: (Sanskrit: महाराज, also spelled maharajah) is a Sanskrit title for a “great ruler”, “great king” or “high king”
